headline_marked: [[Two Local AI Agents]] Build an App With No Human Input
headline: Two Local AI Agents Build an App With No Human Input
summary: An experiment in multi-agent AI systems sees one AI build an app and another review it, with surprising results.
details: A developer tested the capabilities of local AI models by tasking two agents to build an application without human intervention. One agent acted as the 'Builder', creating or modifying code, while the second, the 'Reviewer', inspected the output and requested changes.

The project, named RelayLab, used Python to orchestrate the interaction between two local AI models running via Ollama. Initially, the system faced resource constraints, with both models consuming significant GPU memory, leading to a need for models to unload after each turn.

The experiment also encountered setup issues, including an incomplete Ollama installation that prevented models from running despite appearing to be downloaded. After a proper reinstallation, the agents were able to communicate and begin the development process.

For the first real test, the system was prompted to create a simple website. The Builder agent successfully generated an index.html file, marking a significant milestone in the AI-driven development process.

A challenge arose when the Reviewer agent's feedback, though sensible, didn't conform to the strict enum format expected by the orchestrator, causing a crash. This highlighted the sensitivity of AI models to specific output formats.

The orchestrator was subsequently made more tolerant of variations in status reporting, normalizing terms like 'rejected' and 'approved'. This adjustment allowed the process to continue, though new issues, such as malformed JSON, emerged.

The developer noted the unique satisfaction of running AI models locally and integrating them into a custom system, contrasting it with the experience of using cloud-based services like ChatGPT. The experiment demonstrated the potential of local AI agents in software development workflows.
